title: 54% of US Workers Skip Lunch at Least Once a Week
paragraphs: Do you sometimes skip lunch at work? Many people do.
One thousand US workers were asked about how they eat at work by ezCater, a US food ordering platform. This is the fifth year ezCater has asked workers about their food.

It found that, over the last four years, the number of workers who skip lunch at least once a week has been going up. Fifty-four percent of US workers now say they skip lunch at least once a week, up from 48% in 2023.
And that's not good — because 84% of workers say they don't work as well when they're hungry!
But almost one-third of workers say their company culture makes it hard to take lunch. And 31% say they eat lunch at their desks — but just 16% say they want to eat there.
On average, US workers spend about $100 a week on lunches, down 8% from 2025. But 81% of workers say they have changed how they have lunch because food is getting too expensive.
Many buy lunch at shops and restaurants less often, or choose cheaper food. And 21% now say they look for meals or snacks provided by their company — 38% more than said so in 2025.

Looking at these answers, Robert Kaskel from ezCater said companies could help their people work better — and feel happier — by providing them lunches. He said companies should make giving people food a part of their culture!
